# Python model API with vetiver {#sec-model-vetiver} This chapter is the standalone lab file for the processing layer in [Lab 2](lab02.qmd). Below is the code I included in `_labs/lab02/model-vetiver/model-vetiver.qmd`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(reticulate) use_virtualenv("myenv", required = TRUE) virtualenv_install( envname = "myenv", packages = c("palmerpenguins", "pandas", "numpy", "scikit-learn", "duckdb", "vetiver", "pins")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from palmerpenguins import load_penguins #<1> from pandas import get_dummies import numpy as np from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn import preprocessing import duckdb ``` ::: 1. Added this for the `penguins` data ## Get Data The code below loads the `penguins` data, writes it to a `duckdb` table, and reads it back as a DataFrame without missing values. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} penguins_data = load_penguins() #<1> con = duckdb.connect('my-db.duckdb') con.execute("CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data") #<2> df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM penguins").fetchdf().dropna() con.close() df.head(3) ``` ::: 1. Load the data for the `duckdb` 2. Create the `penguins` table in db ## Define Model and Fit Next, we dummy code `species` and `sex` and fit a linear regression that predicts `body_mass_g`. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} X = get_dummies(df[['bill_length_mm', 'species', 'sex']], drop_first = True) y = df['body_mass_g'] model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y) ``` ::: ## Print model fit statistics The fitted model's R², intercept, columns, and coefficients are printed below. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} print(f"R^2 {model.score(X,y)}") print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}") print(f"Columns {X.columns}") print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}") ``` ::: ## Turn into Vetiver Model `VetiverModel()` wraps the fitted model with its name and prototype data (`X`). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from vetiver import VetiverModel v = VetiverModel(model, model_name='penguin_model', prototype_data=X) ``` ::: ## Save to Board The code below creates a `pins` board in `./models` and writes a versioned copy of the `VetiverModel` to it. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from pins import board_folder from vetiver import vetiver_pin_write model_board = board_folder("./models", allow_pickle_read=True) #<1> vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v) ``` ::: 1. Use the current working directory ## Turn model into API ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from vetiver import VetiverAPI app = VetiverAPI(v, check_prototype = True) ``` ::: ## Recap 1. The `model-vetiver.qmd` file adds `load_penguins()` so the data exists before we query `duckdb`. The `penguins` table is created from that DataFrame, then read back with `fetchdf()` and `dropna()`. 2. The fitted `LinearRegression()` becomes a `VetiverModel()` named `penguin_model`, and `vetiver_pin_write()` saves it to a `board_folder()` in `./models`. Setting `allow_pickle_read=True` lets the board read the pickled `scikit-learn` model back. 3. The last step, `VetiverAPI(v, check_prototype = True)`, turns the pinned model into an API object that checks incoming data against the prototype. Next, [R processing layer](model-vetiver-r.qmd) repeats these steps in R. The original code from lab 2 is below:
View model-vetiver.qmd
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```` --- title: "Model" format: html: code-fold: true --- ```{python} from pandas import get_dummies import numpy as np from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn import preprocessing ``` ## Get Data ```{python} import duckdb con = duckdb.connect('my-db.duckdb') df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM penguins").fetchdf().dropna() con.close() df.head(3) ``` ## Define Model and Fit ```{python} X = get_dummies(df[['bill_length_mm', 'species', 'sex']], drop_first = True) y = df['body_mass_g'] model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y) ``` ## Get some information ```{python} print(f"R^2 {model.score(X,y)}") print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}") print(f"Columns {X.columns}") print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}") ``` ## Turn into Vetiver Model ```{python} from vetiver import VetiverModel v = VetiverModel(model, model_name='penguin_model', prototype_data=X) ``` ## Save to Board ```{python} from pins import board_folder from vetiver import vetiver_pin_write model_board = board_folder("/data/model", allow_pickle_read = True) vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v) ``` ## Turn model into API ```{python} from vetiver import VetiverAPI app = VetiverAPI(v, check_prototype = True) ``` ```` ::: :::
